chapter: Al Hibbler, Dakota Staton and later years
title: Fun with Al Hibbler: train tricks and morning drinks
summary: The blind, jolly Hibbler fakes shivering to board trains early, and they open each morning with scotch and gin.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: I'm trying to think of some of the more significant things that happened with Al Hibbler. I guess altogether it was just a fun thing with Al, because we had a lot of private jokes going.... All is completely without sight. He was born blind and he couldn't see. But he was the kind of guy that you'd never know it, because he's happy-go-lucky, he's always jolly and laughing about something and doing all kinds of wild things.

One of the things I remember, he and I worked together, we would... Perhaps in a situation of catching a train. When I first went with him, he had a fear about riding in planes. So we did a lot of riding on the train. He used to get these expensive bedrooms on the train, and have these very luxurious trips from one place to the other, with all this train service that was afforded back in those days.

Sometimes, when we took short trips on trains, where we'd ride coach, there would be a lot of people lined up getting on these trains. I would tell Al, "Man, we might have to stand up on this particular coach." He said, "Why?" I said, "Because there are a lot of people out here." So he said, "Come on." So we would go and get close up to the door, stand in the crowd, and in the wintertime Al would go into his trembling act, and he would tremble and shiver like he was freezin' to death, and I would be standing there with him. The conductor would look over at me and Al, and he would tell the people, "You people move aside, move aside, move aside. Let this man through here." Now, these people would be waiting to board the train, and we'd always get on the train at least five or ten minutes ahead of time, and get the choice seat that we would want, and all of this. After we'd get on the train, we'd go back annd find a seat and sit down there, and Al would touch me on the side and say, "We made it."

Things like that. We had a lot of fun, laughing. He and I were doing a lot of drinking in those days. Al drank scotch and I drank gin, and we'd always have a fifth with us. We used to open up the mornings by... We'd usually get adjoining rooms or something. We'd get up, and I would say to Al, or he'd say to me, "Have you had yours yet?" I'd say, "No. "Have you had yours?" "No. Okay, let's go together." And we'd
turn the bottle open, take the drink, and then we'd make all kinds of commotion about how it felt for about a minute, then we'd sit down and say, "Boy, it sure was good, wasn't it."
